domain_guidance.summary: This domain focuses on the antepartum period, accounting for 21.0% of the exam. It covers the identification of risk factors, maternal health assessment, and the management of pregnancy-related conditions to ensure outcomes for the patient and fetus.

Covering 21.0% of the exam, this domain addresses intrapartum care. It includes the management of labor, delivery maneuvers, and the identification of obstetric emergencies like shoulder dystocia to prevent neonatal and maternal morbidity during the birth process.

This domain represents 18.0% of the exam and centers on postpartum care. It involves the assessment of maternal recovery, identification of complications, and the provision of support following the delivery process to ensure health and safety.

Accounting for 10.0% of the exam, this domain covers newborn care. It focuses on the immediate evaluation of the infant, transition to extrauterine life, and identification of potential health issues following birth to support neonatal well-being.

This domain makes up 19.0% of the exam and addresses gynecology. It involves the provision of gynecological health services, including routine screenings, diagnosis, and management of common reproductive health conditions within the scope of midwifery practice.

Representing 11.0% of the exam, this domain covers primary care. It focuses on the broader health needs of patients, including health promotion, disease prevention, and the management of general health concerns within the scope of midwifery practice.

editorial.overview: The Certified Nurse-Midwife Examination is administered by the American Midwifery Certification Board (AMCB). This certification evaluates clinical proficiency across six primary domains: Antepartum, Intrapartum, Postpartum, Newborn, Gynecology, and Primary Care. It assesses the knowledge required for safe and effective midwifery practice, ensuring that candidates can manage various clinical scenarios, including obstetric emergencies and routine care, in accordance with established professional standards for nurse-midwives seeking to demonstrate their competency in the field.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the six domains, which carry weights ranging from 10.0% to 21.0%. Focus on the clinical management of obstetric complications, such as shoulder dystocia, and understand the anatomy and physiology of the pelvic girdle. Utilize official resources from the American Midwifery Certification Board (AMCB) to align your study with the exam's structure. Practice identifying risk factors and applying appropriate maneuvers for delivery complications to ensure you are prepared for the assessment.
editorial.who_should_take: This examination is intended for individuals who have successfully completed an accredited nurse-midwifery education program and are seeking professional certification. Candidates should possess the clinical knowledge and skills necessary to provide care for patients across the entire reproductive lifespan and newborn health.
